interfaces.name: Wrike Workspace (web application, also delivered as a Windows/Mac desktop client)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating views, menus and forms of a persistent, navigable representation of workspace state. The desktop client presents the same affordance-manipulation contract and is folded in.

provenance.evidence: Wrike's product surfaces (browser, desktop, mobile) for accessing the workspace.
Desktop app offers largely the same functionality as the browser, confirming the same interaction contract.

interfaces.name: Wrike mobile app (iOS/Android)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Native touch-based client whose interaction contract genuinely differs from the web workspace; actions are expressed by manipulating on-screen affordances.

provenance.evidence: First-party native Android and iOS apps.
Mobile clients for phones and tablets to review and update work.

interfaces.name: Wrike REST API v4
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations via RESTful GET/POST/PUT/DELETE requests under a fixed base with OAuth 2.0.

provenance.evidence: RESTful methods with OAuth 2.0 authorization; base https://www.wrike.com/api/v4.

interfaces.name: Wrike DataHub Public API
interfaces.classification_rationale: Distinct API surface (own OpenAPI, different base and control structure with requestId idempotency and session page tokens) through which the consumer invokes operations on DataHub databases, fields and records.

provenance.evidence: Separate DataHub public API with its own entities and operation set.
OpenAPI servers under www.wrike.com/app/wrike_v2_web with /public/api/v1 paths.

interfaces.name: Email-to-Wrike (inbound task creation/editing)
interfaces.technology: Email (SMTP) submission to a Wrike address
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer invokes the create/edit-task operation by submitting a structured email (subject-line syntax for title, location, dates, status). Structured command via SMTP, not natural-language interpretation, so Programmatic rather than Conversational.

provenance.evidence: Create tasks by emailing a Wrike address with bracketed subject-line parameters.
Send email to Wrike address to create/assign tasks; attachments become task files.

interfaces.name: Wrike Webhooks
interfaces.classification_rationale: The service initiates the interaction when subscribed events occur and delivers a payload to a consumer-controlled hookUrl, rather than the consumer polling.

provenance.evidence: Folder/space/account webhooks push payloads to the client endpoint on specific changes.

interfaces.name: Wrike MCP Server
interfaces.technology: MCP server (Streamable HTTP; OAuth or Permanent Access Token)
interfaces.classification_rationale: A first-party MCP endpoint exposes a fixed, discoverable tool set that AI clients enumerate and select by goal as part of the interaction contract. Capability discovery and selection are part of the contract, so Agentic rather than Programmatic.

provenance.evidence: Wrike MCP server at https://mcp.wrike.com/v2 exposing a fixed tool set clients discover and cache.

interfaces.name: Wrike Copilot
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer interacts through natural-language questions interpreted by the service, with tool orchestration internal to Wrike. Message is the primitive, so Conversational rather than Agentic.

provenance.evidence: Wrike Copilot is an AI assistant built into projects that answers questions and summarizes work on demand.
Copilot uses natural language to get answers and insights; the user simply asks.

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Accessed via the REST API v4 /data-export method (same base and auth); not a separate interface.
First-party integrations built on the API and web UI, not a distinct provider interface.
Specification implemented by external DAM vendors so Wrike can call them; reverse direction, not a way to access Wrike.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: AI Agents / Conversational AI Agent Builder
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: In-product automation and a builder inside the Workspace, not a distinct access interface.
Same affordance-manipulation contract as the web Workspace; folded into it.
No first-party CLI or TUI found in official sources.
Input modality of the mobile app / Copilot, not a distinct interaction contract.
Narrow data-export utility riding on the export API, not a general interaction interface.
Implement the REST API; not interfaces.
